answer: Hypothesis (data-grounded): Effectively all studies in the Experimental Economics (ee) replication project were conducted in a lab setting. In the meta-regression study data, the ee subset comprises 18 unique original/replication pairs (ids ee.1–ee.18), each a single row, with no missing values in any setting-relevant field. Every original experiment was administered in person rather than online (online.o = 0 for 18/18), and the subject pools — 17 pairs with student subjects and 1 (ee.4) with community subjects, and student subjects in all 18 replications — are consistent with physical laboratory experiments. Under the primary rule (lab setting inferred from online.o == 0, since online is the only setting proxy in the data), the proportion of Experimental Economics studies conducted in a lab setting is 18/18 = 100%. Sensitivity checks leave this unchanged: using the replication side (online.r == 0) also gives 18/18 = 100%, and requiring either the original or the replication to be offline gives 18/18 = 100%. Only a strict rule that additionally requires original-study subjects to be students (excluding ee.4's community subjects, which is still offline) lowers the estimate to 17/18 ≈ 94.4%. Caveat: the dataset contains no explicit lab/field indicator, so "lab" is inferred from offline administration; offline does not strictly prove a physical lab (an in-person field experiment is a theoretical possibility), though the student-subject composition makes lab administration the strongly supported reading. The proportion is robust to NA handling (no setting-relevant missingness in ee) and to row exclusions (drop = False for all 18).

Proportion = 18/18 = 100% (lab inferred from online.o == 0, the only available setting proxy); robust at 100% using replication-side or either-side offline rules, and 17/18 ≈ 94.4% under a strict students-only rule (ee.4 uses community subjects but is still offline). Caveat: offline is a proxy — no explicit lab/field column exists, and offline does not strictly prove a physical lab, though student subjects make lab administration strongly supported.
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded meta-regression_study_data CSV (927 rows x 57 cols) and filtered project == 'ee' with drop == False: 18 rows, 18 unique O/R pair ids (ee.1–ee.18), one row per pair, lab_id entirely NaN (no lab-level rows), zero missingness in online.o/r, subjects.o/r, experiment_country.o. 2) Verified the second CSV's 18 'Experimental Economics' studies match the 18 ee ids. 3) Primary classification: lab setting = (online.o == 0) for the original experiment. 4) Sensitivity analyses: (a) online.r == 0 → 18/18; (b) either O or R offline → 18/18; (c) offline AND subjects.o == 'students' → 17/18 = 94.4% (ee.4 = community subjects, still offline). 5) Reported headline proportion with counts and the offline-proxy caveat. Script: analysis_ee_lab_setting.py (executed, output shown in evidence).
